summary: Follow-up to the 8/17 outage: root cause appears to be KV-cache exhaustion combined with an autoscaler race that caused a high number of cold model spins. Redwood and Mistral agreed on immediate mitigations (increase cache thresholds, throttle ingress, patch autoscaler), monitoring improvements, and a runbook/canary rollout schedule.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: hi everyone thanks for joining, we're on 48 minutes, quick agenda: share final RCA, agree mitigations and schedule follow-up.
[00:14] Rachel Kim: thanks Samira, appreciate it. Marcus and Priya are here. we got hit pretty hard yesterday, customer-facing latency spiked and some requests 504'd.
[00:26] Diego Ramos: OK so quick recap from our side, timeline's in the doc, at 02:03 UTC we saw a sustained prefix cache miss spike, kv cache evictions ramped, that caused higher memory pressure and the autoscaler started launching pods but there was a race where a few requests queued and retried which amplified load.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: yeah that's what our traces show, multiple retries from the app layer. question though, is this from batching behaving differently or a kernel issue on the gpus?
[00:57] Diego Ramos: it's primarily cache + autoscaler race. batching looked normal, kernels were fine but we did see increased kernel eviction times on the older drivers; also a small number of nodes went into OOM kill but not many.
[01:12] Priya Nair: and from security standpoint we need to confirm no PII was leaked to logs, and confirm audit logs cover the timeline.
[01:20] Liu Chen: we already ran a quick audit, logs show only control-plane events and we redacted request bodies in the shared bucket; we'll include a full log export.
[01:29] Rachel Kim: can you repeat the autoscaler race explanation? I heard "race" but want to be clear on root cause.
[01:36] Diego Ramos: sure sorry, tl;dr: autoscaler uses pod readiness and queue depth to scale. under heavy eviction we had a path where readiness probes returned slow and the controller launched additional pods but the KV cache wasn't warmed for new pods so they served lots of cache misses, causing increased request latency which then triggered more scale actions. So feedback loop.
[02:05] Samira Patel: and that feedback loop is what pushed latency into the customer-visible window. we also detected that prefix caching threshold config was lower than we'd expected in the customer config - that made warming slower.
[02:20] Marcus Lee: ah, config drift. we did change the cache params in april, maybe not synced. who owns config sync?
[02:26] Rachel Kim: infra team owns it, but we use terraform and sometimes manual edits happen during incident response, bad process.
[02:35] Samira Patel: action item to pin recommended cache thresholds in prod config and include as part of managed deploys.
[02:40] Diego Ramos: short term mitigations we propose: 1) increase KV cache max entries and eviction grace, 2) add circuit-breaker to ingress to limit retries, 3) patch autoscaler to consider warm-cache metric before adding pods, 4) driver update on a small canary to address kernel eviction anomalies.
[03:00] Priya Nair: for security/compliance, we need confirmation that audit logs are immutable and KMS keys weren't rotated during the window.
[03:10] Liu Chen: KMS rotations are on a strict schedule, none occurred that hour; audit logs were generated and we can provide hash-signed copies. we'll attach to the postmortem doc.
[03:20] Marcus Lee: what's the rollback plan if the autoscaler patch has unexpected behavior?
[03:24] Diego Ramos: we'll do canary rollout on the Dedicated pool first with a 10% traffic slice, monitoring CPU/GPU queue depth and latency; rollback will be automatic if latency or error rate crosses thresholds.
[03:36] Samira Patel: note that Mistral is currently on Dedicated but also has Redwood Private trial in staging, correct?
[03:42] Rachel Kim: yes staging is Private, prod is Dedicated. we want the reliability improvements to apply to both.
[03:48] Samira Patel: agreed. long-term improvements: smarter batching, enhanced prefix caching heuristics, telemetry for warm-cache rate, alerting on sustained miss-rate and autoscaler-loop detection.
[04:02] Marcus Lee: can we get a metric that shows "cache-warm-rate" per model and per pool? that would help us set SLAs.
[04:08] Diego Ramos: yes we can expose that in Redwood Console; Diego to add dashboard tile and alert rule.
[04:15] Rachel Kim: on the customer side we want a runbook step for throttling the app layer to avoid retries — we'll add that.
[04:22] Samira Patel: ok recap of owners: Diego will share metrics/logs, Liu will update runbook and share PR, Samira will send pricing/credits note. Customer to share traces. we schedule runbook review 8/21.
[04:33] Priya Nair: quick question: SOC2 documentation — can you share the cert and any relevant audit points for the control plane that we can add to our compliance folder?
[04:40] Liu Chen: yes, we will attach latest SOC2 Type II and a short note on our logging/audit controls; also share our DPA.
[04:48] Marcus Lee: timeline of expected patching?
[04:50] Diego Ramos: autoscaler patch: initial PR this week, testing early next week, canary 8/24, full rollout 8/28 assuming no regressions. driver/canary and config pinning earlier — we can do driver canary 8/20.
[05:05] Rachel Kim: sounds good. one more ask: can Redwood run a synthetic load test that mirrors our traffic pattern before the canary?
[05:11] Samira Patel: yes we'll run a tailored load test and share results, Diego will own.
[05:16] Marcus Lee: great. anything else?
[05:18] Samira Patel: nope, thanks everyone. we'll follow-up with the timeline and artifacts.
[05:22] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors (e.g., "kv" typed as "k v" in places), speaker attributions may not align perfectly with exact speaker turns.
